_comment: Rio's agent rules. One entry per rule Rio wants enforced mechanically
instead of hoping prose in AGENTS.md lands. See README.md for the schema.
on     'tool'     - checked before a tool runs  (Claude PreToolUse)
'response' - checked on the final reply   (Claude/Codex Stop)
match  regexes. 'tool'/'input' for on=tool, 'text' for on=response.
Omitted keys match anything. All present keys must match.
unless regex escape hatch; matches -> rule is skipped this time.
do     'remind' - non-blocking nudge into the agent's context
'deny'   - block the tool call outright (on=tool only)
text   what the agent is told. Say the rule AND what to do instead.

rules.text: BLOCKED: UI tests can take over Rio's desktop. Before launching, inspect the actual config and launch helper. Prefix this one command with RIO_UI_TEST_MODE=headless only for a verified headless run (Electron is visible even without --headed); approved only after Rio explicitly approves this visible run; or isolated only after verifying the target is unused and cannot steal focus/input from his active desktop. A second monitor or Space alone is not isolation. For any visible run, have a bounded timeout and an independent stop command ready first. Never bypass this gate through another tool or wrapper. If safety is unknown, keep working headlessly or ask Rio.

Rio prefers `trash` over `rm`, deletions stay recoverable. This command is allowed and will run. Use `rm` only when it is genuinely right: CI cleanup, temp/build artifacts, or a path Trash cannot handle.

Your reply mentions a fallback. Rio's code style is FAIL FAST AND LOUD, no fallbacks. If you added one, remove it and let the failure surface. If you were only describing or rejecting a fallback, say so plainly and stop.

Blocked: a pipe hides git push's exit code, so a push the pre-push hook refused ends with exit 0 and gets reported as done. Run `git push` unpiped; its output is short. If you must pipe it, start the command with `set -o pipefail;`.

This writes hand-drawn SVG. Rio's rule: never author icons, logos, or vector art by hand. they look off. Use an icon library (lucide, heroicons, simple-icons) or his real assets in `~/Documents/Graphic Design/Logos:Icons/`. If this SVG is a copy-paste from one of those sources, carry on.

BLOCKED: this looks like a hand-rolled dev-server start. Rio's rule: never guess how to run an app. Run `dev-up` instead -- it finds the repo's start script, runs it through portless as a named pm2 process, waits until the app answers, and prints the tailnet URL. That is the whole job; do not inspect ports, processes, or other worktrees first. If dev-up exits 2 (no start script), say so and offer to add one. If it exits 1, read the log tail it printed, report the cause, and recommend the one-shot fix. If the command you were about to run IS the repo's own start script, re-run it prefixed with `RIO_RUN_OK=1 `.

Blocked: piping a full pytest run through tail/grep throws away most of its output, and agents then rerun the whole suite (about a minute) just to see more. Run it once into a file and read the file: `pytest -q > "$TMPDIR/pytest.log" 2>&1; echo exit=$?`, then grep/tail the log. Piping is fine for focused runs (a test file, `::`, `-k`, `--lf`). If a pre-push hook runs the suite, skip the full run before pushing.

Partial read of a past session: peek, --human-only, or `show` filtered or cut short. Fine for finding sessions, not for saying what was asked, decided, done, or why. Before answering or reporting that, read `session-handoff show <key>` end to end; if it truncates, save it to a file and read the file in order. In your answer or report, say which sessions you read in full and which only partially.

Your reply puts a decision to Rio. Only decision ladder step 4 (versions built and running, his pick queued, work continues) or step 5 (hard to undo, a big rewrite if wrong, risky: merge, spend, prod data, lost work, or a load-bearing departure from the standard) may reach him, plus a yes a skill or rule requires before work starts (captain's contract, plan approval, big-work scope). Tiny and easy to undo? Make the obvious call, label it in the code if off-standard, and report it in one line. A real step 4, step 5, or required yes? Keep it, add a plain `Why you: <reason>` line, and give your pick plus 1-2 alternatives. This bounce is never his yes: work that waits on his approval keeps waiting, and a confused reply from him means explain again, not start. Headless step 5 goes to the ask queue instead. Not a question at all? Drop the ❓.

Rio set attention to away for this session: nobody will answer, so never end on a question to him. Take the safest reversible path and keep working to done or budget. A real step-5 decision goes to the PM inbox as an `- ask:` line (headless rule); carry on with whatever does not depend on it. Work that needs his yes first (plan approval, big-work scope) waits for it: queue the ask, never treat silence as approval. Nothing irreversible meanwhile.
